advice: I abstain. The supplied evidence covers the distinct legal loop orders available in the current source: the original 64-row-block traversal, row-half-first traversal, column-panel-first traversal, and the panel32 row-band wrapper. Each changed order was measured and unpromoted. Another row/column interchange would repeat one of those experiments. A different panel shape needs a generated helper that is not supplied. I know no distinct, useful loop-order change that the current source can support without new generated shapes.
risks: Do not infer that loop order caused any score changes or that another order will improve throughput. If a new helper becomes available, verify its pointer, leading-dimension, and output mapping; check the full k reduction, every output, the general-size and tail paths, n<=0, ABI, and complete license notice. Any changed source needs fresh paired measurements under the unchanged benchmark and power settings.
